papers.title: Release Kinetics and Mechanical Adaptation of Stimuli-Responsive and 3D-Printed Hydrogels: A Reproducible Meta-Analysis of Tabulated Open-Access Data
papers.abstract: Stimuli-responsive hydrogels are expected to change their drug release and stiffness when pH, temperature, enzymes, magnetic fields or light change, and 3D printing is increasingly used to shape them, yet whether these effects are consistent across studies has not been quantified. We built a reproducible dataset by querying Europe PMC for CC BY articles and parsing the tables of 4601 full-text XML records programmatically. 33 studies (9 printed) contributed 220 reported Korsmeyer-Peppas exponents (n), 19 release profiles and 47 modulus values. Re-fitting five release models to the profiles showed that no model dominated; the Weibull function had the smallest median ΔAIC (1.9). Reported exponents had a median of 0.54 (IQR 0.37 to 0.69), indicating mostly anomalous (56%) or Fickian (40%) transport. Stimulus classes differed at record level (Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.001) but not when each study was represented once (p = 0.47). Within studies, raising pH lowered n in 7 of 9 pH-responsive systems (median Δn = -0.048, Wilcoxon p < 0.001), whereas magnetic and enzyme triggers gave no consistent shift. Temperature stiffened poloxamer thermogels by two to four orders of magnitude, and printing light dose and polymer concentration tuned moduli log-linearly. A random forest using design descriptors did not beat a mean predictor under leave-one-study-out validation (R² = -0.19). Release mechanism therefore depends more on the individual formulation than on the stimulus class, and standardised reporting of raw release and mechanical data is needed before predictive design is feasible.

papers.title: A Predictive and Adaptive CPCEIF Framework for Efficient Computing in Heterogeneous Environments
papers.abstract: The rise in the number of programming languages and software tools has added to the complexity involved in code editing and software development collaboration. Aside from tools, there are significant issues constituting cloud computing technologies and software and operating systems which aggravate the issue even further. Today there are different platforms for programming languages such as Java, Python, C/C++, C#, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go etc. to exist at the same time. Despite the existence of many code editors and programming languages concurrent with the development of language servers, there are still interoperability problems to be resolved in relation to working with different platforms. Differences in the structure and functionality of programming languages, APIs, communication protocols, data formats, authentication, structure and dependencies lead to platform reliance, inconsistent results, synchronization delay and an overall requirement for greater effort. This paper highlights that CPCEIF (Cross-Programming-Language Code Editing Interoperability Framework) is a solution that eliminates the issue by means of the use of an abstraction layer while programming languages are used by means of programming tools. Additionally, the Framework offers synchronization and compatibilities. The CPCEIF architecture has a modular and extensible architecture that permits the assimilation of new programming languages, platforms, APIs and development environments without altering the system's architectural structure significantly. Therefore, different trial approaches will be utilized to verify the prototype implementation and guarantee the variety of the operators' elements. The analysis will focus on such parameters as the rates of interoperability effectiveness and various aspects of them including consistency of programming, efficiency of synchronization, correctness of conversion, transmission delay, integration costs, scalability and efficacy of utilization of resources.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Adaptive Clustering for Energy-Efficient Wireless Sensor Networks: A Mathematical Approach
papers.abstract: Energy balancing is an important challenge in wireless sensor networks (WSNs). The challenges of WSNs are considerable in terms of maintaining a balanced energy utilization and extending the network lifetime, especially because of the need to operate the networks for extended periods of time without any human intervention and the energy constraints. We introduce A2C-WSN, a novel mathematical framework that integrates machine learning based cluster head (CH) selection and constrained optimization to realize a deterministic energy-balanced clustering. The AI-assisted model used a decision tree classification method for choosing the appropriate cluster heads using the normalized energy value. Then, the A2C-WSN framework used a greedy approach to select the location of the cluster head with a given cluster cardinality. A maximum energy-weighted utility function was also optimized to further optimize energy distribution throughout the network. The A2C-WSN was evaluated when compared with the existing WSN protocols such as LEACH and Energy Aware protocols at various network sizes, N = 50, 100, 150 and 200. The results showed that A2C-WSN has competitive half-node death (HND) performance. In particular, A2C-WSN performed at a higher HND (809 rounds) than Energy Aware (802 rounds), with only a 0.9% difference. Additionally, A2C-WSN successfully transmitted 8.5% more packets than LEACH, and this could be because of the deterministic selection of CH in each round. The ablation study showed that the optimization module helped reduce the death of the last node (LND) by 16.1% compared to uncontrolled choice of CH. Apart from that, cross validation indicated an accuracy of 99.66% ± 0.12% for the classifier. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis showed that the weights on the input features did not significantly affect the performance of the classifier as the difference in LND was less than one round with weights w1 ranging from 0.1 to 0.9. Besides, the computational time of A2C-WSN framework is moderate, which took 18.2 s for 1600 times simulation of all three protocols. The mathematical model offers a promising solution for sustainable IoT applications with predictable and balanced energy management. This work is based on previous clustering research in WSNs and also shows that hybrid approaches of combining machine learning with optimization techniques can successfully combine theoretical guarantees with practical performance enhancements.

papers.title: Modifying structure and properties of CoCrCuxNiMoy (x = 0, 0.1, y = 0.1, 0.5, 1) MPEAs by chemical composition and laser-surface treatment
papers.abstract: In this work, the structure and selected properties like corrosion resistance and hardness of CoCrCu x NiMo y (x = 0, 0.1, y = 0.1, 0.5, 1) alloys in the as-cast state and after laser surface treatment were characterized. The structural investigations confirmed that with a higher molybdenum addition, the ability to form a dual-phase structure composed of the FCC and the intermetallic phase increases, which leads to a decrease in corrosion resistance, but increases hardness. The addition of copper turned out to be beneficial for a single-phase CoCrCu 0.1 NiMo 0.1 alloy due to the best electrochemical parameters ( R p = 244 kΩcm 2 , j corr = 0.55 μA/cm 2 − as-cast state, R p = 320 kΩcm 2 , j corr = 0.04 μA/cm 2 − after laser surface treatment). In the dual-phase alloys, the FCC phase was enriched in copper, which led to higher Volta potential differences that promoted corrosion. Laser surface treatment resulted in grain refinement in the structure. Single-phase CoCrNiMo 0.1 alloy after laser surface treatment showed improved corrosion resistance and increased hardness compared to the as-cast state form. However, the CoCrCu 0.1 NiMo 0.1 alloy after laser surface treatment was characterized by the presence of copper-rich precipitates resulting lower corrosion resistance. The improvement in corrosion resistance and increased hardness depended on the share of the FCC and intermetallic phase.

papers.title: Salvianolic Acid-A/Gemcitabine loaded hydrogel reprograms the immunosuppressive microenvironment and inhibits bladder cancer progression by targeting mTOR/STAT3/IL-10 pathway
papers.abstract: The clinical management of bladder cancer, particularly intravesical chemotherapy, is severely hampered by rapid drug wash-out and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. To address these limitations, we developed an injectable thermosensitive PLGA-PEG-PLGA hydrogel co-loaded with salvianolic acid A (SAA) and gemcitabine (GEM) as a localized drug delivery system. The hydrogel exhibited a rapid sol–gel transition at physiological body temperature and enabled sustained co-release of GEM and SAA for over 13 days in physiological media. As a proof-of-concept (PoC), localized administration of the co-loaded hydrogel in a subcutaneous murine bladder cancer model significantly augmented the therapeutic efficacy of GEM while reducing the required chemotherapy dosage. Mechanistic investigations demonstrated that SAA suppressed tumor-derived IL-10 sretion via the mTOR/STAT3 axis, thereby blocking M2 macrophage polarization and enhancing pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage infiltration. This targeted immune reprogramming restructured the M2-predominant immunosuppressive macrophage microenvironment into a pro-inflammatory state, consequently enhancing cellular GEM uptake by tumor cells. Overall, this dual-drug hydrogel platform integrates localized sustained release with macrophage-targeted microenvironment reprogramming, offering a promising strategy for synergistic chemo-immunotherapy against bladder cancer.

papers.title: Targeted nanomedicine for ischemic cardiomyopathy
papers.abstract: Ischemic cardiomyopathy remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. The therapeutic efficacy of conventional pharmacological interventions is constrained by poor bioavailability, limited myocardial targeting capacity, and systemic adverse effects. Nanomedicine has emerged as a promising strategy to overcome these limitations by enhancing drug stability, prolonging blood circulation time, and enabling precise delivery to diseased tissues. In the setting of ischemic cardiomyopathy, active targeting approaches-particularly those functionalized with tannic acid and cardiac-targeting peptides-have been extensively investigated to boost the delivery efficiency of therapeutic agents and halt disease progression. Moreover, the ischemic microenvironment (IME), characterized by inflammation, redox imbalance, and enzymatic dysregulation, not only drives pathological progression but also creates unique opportunities for site-specific therapeutic intervention. Systematic comprehension and evaluation of these targeting strategies are critical to advancing the clinical translation of myocardium-targeted nanomedicines. In this review, we summarize recent advances in myocardium-targeted nanotherapeutic strategies, with a special focus on tannic acid-based systems, cardiac-targeting peptides, reductive microenvironment-responsive platforms, and enzyme-responsive delivery approaches. We also discuss the current limitations and future perspectives of such strategies, aiming to offer insights into the rational design and clinical development of next-generation therapeutics for ischemic cardiomyopathy.

papers.title: Factors determining the enzymatic degradation of PLA/PHBV blends
papers.abstract: Blends of poly(lactic acid) and poly(hydroxybutyrat-co-valerate) were prepared in the entire composition range to compensate the deficiencies of the components and prepare materials with optimal properties including biodegradability. The polymers were homogenized by extrusion and then injection molded into plates with different thickness to study its effect on enzymatic degradation. Five enzymes were selected for the preliminary study, and then degradation was followed as a function of time. Many factors influence the degradation of injection-molded specimens. Besides composition, the crystallinity and structure of PHBV proved to be the main factors determining the rate and extent of degradation. Structure is very complex including skin-core morphology, orientation, surface area, and the differences in the structure of injection molded and cut surfaces. PLA and PHBV are immiscible, and their blends have a heterogeneous dispersed structure, but the interaction of the two components is not negligible, and thus influences both structure and degradation. Enzymatic degradation proceeds in three steps and the modeling of degradation kinetics together with the analysis of the dependence of the parameters helps the identification and understanding of the factors influencing degradation. In this study, basically only PLA degrades in the blends and the presence of PHBV controls its degradation.
